Examples cover angle-to-amount, percent-to-angle, bar comparison against a mean, decoding an unlabeled halfway tick, interpreting scatter association without cause, percent increase, and comparing truncated and zero-based scales. The cases add distinct reasoning and reach multi-step interpretation.
All multi-step worked solutions use numbered steps; key calculations are displayed and no solving step is omitted.
Display equations are split into short arithmetic or single-formula lines suitable for a phone.
Teaching paragraphs contain at most three sentences; there are no long bullet lists.

Every FIGURE marker is a one-line chart specification with labels or descriptive semantics. Both ILLUSTRATION markers specify axes, data, ticks, and bar endpoints; #7 includes the axis break. Text independently describes all required graph information.

Sector, share decimal, axis, tick steps, truncated axis, mean, percent-change symbols, scatter dots, linear association, correlation, and causation are explained before the examples. No prerequisite teaching is assumed for these methods.

The lesson explains pie parts as fractions of a whole, bar height as values, step size from equal intervals, mean as sum divided by count, truncation as omitted scale, and scatter patterns without proof of cause.

Scale steps require equal spaces; percent change uses a positive starting value. Truncation affects appearance but not values; no straight pattern can still hide a curve; observed association does not establish causation.
Both flagged marks phrases refer to graph tick marks. Neither denotes scores; there are no app questions called cards.
